gates.structural_note: Five rounds. Three of the five regressions were caused by the fix from the round before, and all three were in the same enumeration. The pattern list is being asked to make a semantic distinction - person, institution, instrument or indicator - that it cannot represent. Nothing here is unsafe: no unresolved P0 or P1, both directions pinned by tests at every round, and every remaining over-block recorded with the cost of its repair. But the next round should not be a sixth patch. The honest options are a subject-classification step or a measured, documented false-positive rate. Not a change to make inside a release-candidate freeze.

closure_conditions.where_the_closing_verdict_lives: docs/REVIEW_ATTESTATION.json and .md are the only review paths on the RC preflight's evidence-only allowlist, so the CLOSING gate - the one that finds nothing needing a code change - is recorded there rather than here. This file records the gates that produced fixes, and each of those commits lands before the candidate it precedes.
closure_conditions.pattern_worth_noting: Four rounds, four times the fix introduced or left a defect, and three of those four were in the same enumeration. The guardrail is a pattern list being asked to make a semantic distinction, and each round buys coverage at the price of a false positive somewhere else. Recorded here because the next round should weigh a different approach against a fifth patch, not because the current state is unsafe: no unresolved P0 or P1 remains at any gate.
closure_conditions.what_changed_at_gate_f: Rounds B through E each replaced one pattern with a slightly different pattern, and the regression rate stayed flat. Gate F's promise fix changed what the rule keys on - subject rather than object - and collapsed four branches into two while fixing the finding. That is the first evidence in this chain that the surface can converge rather than oscillate, and it is the reason the next round is worth running as a review rather than as a redesign.

reading_rule: A gate entry records what a review found at one SHA. No gate entry ever makes its own SHA clean: a review that produced fixes is evidence AGAINST the SHA it examined. A clean candidate is one where a gate found nothing needing a code change, and only docs/REVIEW_ATTESTATION.json asserts that, checked against the commit graph by the RC preflight. UNKNOWN stays UNKNOWN.
